page: Microsoft Azure M64ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv4 family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. It is provisioned with 1024.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a high density ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. The instance includes no onboard GPUs and comes without local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of remote Premium Storage volumes for disk-dependent operations.

The 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio targets environments that demand substantial working memory without scaling out core counts excessively. Because the server features dedicated CPU allocation, it maintains steady compute capacity without hypervisor contention. However, the complete absence of local ephemeral NVMe or SSD storage means all paging, swap, and disk I/O depend directly on remote block storage network performance.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high memory density allows consolidation of large memory footprints onto a single node, reducing administrative complexity and inter-node networking overhead relative to multi-instance clusters. The hardware layout makes the M64ls_v4 appropriate for massive in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) suites, large analytical processing systems, and high-capacity caching layers that require up to a terabyte of working memory.
description: Microsoft Azure M64ls_v4 is a memory-optimized instance from the MSMediumMemoryv4 family, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs built on an x86_64 Intel architecture. Managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, operating as a diskless compute node that relies on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file systems and ephemeral paging. With its 1:16 processor-to-memory ratio, the configuration is structured to eliminate compute-side overprovisioning when hosting workloads defined primarily by large memory footprints. The M64ls_v4 is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, SAP systems, and big data analytics platforms needing significant volatile memory headroom.
